newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber untraded, buying seen slim.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber untraded, buying seen slim.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midsession on Friday with the trade uncertain whether Michelin would buy fresh supplies of RSS3 rubber in the afternoon session, dealers said.
"It's pretty quiet. I suppose we'll have to wait for Japan to get some fresh leads in trading later in the day," a dealer said.
Traders said a holiday on Monday in Japan and Thailand, the world's biggest producer of natural rubber, weighed on sentiment and kept most people sidelined in the morning.

"I don't know if Michelin will still buy with the holidays coming up. My feeling is they will probably wait for next week," a dealer said. Other dealers said Michelin might want to pick up more material if they find prices of RSS3 to their liking.
Michelin's has been buying RSS3 rubber over the past four days. Bridgestone bought some TSR20 rubber earlier in the week, but has not been active lately.
At around 0430 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 92.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 93.00 cents. October TSR20 was seen at 99.00 U.S. cents a kg from 99.50 cents.
